# INVESTMENT MEMORANDUM
**PetIQ Holdings, LLC - First Amendment Agreement**

---

## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

**Date of Agreement:** February 3, 2023

**Borrower/Company Overview:** PetIQ, LLC, an Idaho limited liability company, serves as the borrower under this credit facility. The company is owned by PetIQ Holdings, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company.

**Transaction Description:** This transaction represents a first amendment to an existing ABL (Asset-Based Lending) Credit and Guaranty Agreement originally dated April 13, 2021. The amendment involves PetIQ Holdings, LLC, PetIQ, LLC (borrower), multiple guarantor subsidiaries, and a syndicate of lenders including KeyBank National Association (as Administrative Agent), The Huntington National Bank, and Comerica Bank.

**Purpose of Financing:** The amendment primarily facilitates the conversion of existing LIBOR-based loans to SOFR (Secured Overnight Financing Rate) loans, with the borrower not required to pay breakage fees in connection with this conversion. The amendment also modifies certain provisions of the original credit agreement.

**Company Background:** Based on the guarantor subsidiaries listed, PetIQ operates in the pet care industry through various entities including Community Veterinary Clinics, Sergeant's Pet Care Products, VIP Petcare, and other pet health and pharmaceutical brands. The company appears to have a diversified portfolio spanning veterinary services, pet pharmaceuticals, and pet care products.

---

## 2. INVESTMENT HIGHLIGHTS & RISKS

**Key Strengths/Credit Positives:**
• Diversified business model across multiple pet care verticals (veterinary clinics, pharmaceuticals, pet care products)
• Established credit relationship with original facility dating to April 2021
• Strong guarantor support from 16+ subsidiary entities across the platform
• Proactive transition from LIBOR to SOFR demonstrating operational sophistication
• Multi-bank syndicate providing diversified funding sources

**Principal Risks and Mitigating Factors:**
• Limited financial performance visibility - no financial metrics or covenant details provided in amendment
• Complex corporate structure with multiple subsidiary guarantors may create operational complexity
• Asset-based lending structure suggests potential working capital or cash flow constraints
• Pet care industry exposure to consumer discretionary spending and economic cycles
• *Mitigating Factor:* Established banking relationships with reputable regional and national lenders
